summary: The appellant, Honnaiah T.H., challenged the High Court's dismissal of his criminal revision petition, which sought to have his statement marked as an exhibit in the trial. The trial court and High Court held the order declining to mark the statement as interlocutory and non-maintainable under Section 397(2) CrPC. The Supreme Court held that the order substantially affected the prosecution's case, as the appellant's statement formed the basis of the FIR, and thus was not merely interlocutory. It concluded that the High Court erred in dismissing the revision on grounds of maintainability and that such an order could result in a miscarriage of justice.
legal_provisions_cited: Amar Nath v State of Haryana
KK Patel v State of Gujarat
Madhu Limaye v State of Maharashtra
Rajendra Kumar Sitaram Pande v Uttam
final_judgment: The appeal was allowed, the High Court's order was set aside, and the revision petition was remanded to be decided on merits.
